governance_policy.aggregation_prohibition_rule: Platform code must never calculate weighted sums or mathematical averages across risk domains. Unified risk profile provides categorical priorities, attention levels, and qualitative synthesis.
fail_closed_rules: Prohibited leakage features fail closed with 422.
NaN, Inf, or unhandled null in required model features fail closed.
Unavailable domains return probability=null and operational_decision=null.
Structurally ineligible records return status=INELIGIBLE and probability=null.
Unknown domains or contradictory regimes fail closed.
Uncalibrated models must not falsely claim calibration.
governance_policy.ineligibility_rules: When a project record belongs to a segment that structurally omits target telemetry (e.g. Segments 1 & 2 for implementation risk), status is INELIGIBLE with null probability and deterministic, machine-readable reason.
governance_policy.non_causal_explanation_rule: All explanations are strictly non-causal statistical associations. Platform consumers must display explanations with non_causal=true metadata and warning disclaimers.
governance_policy.unavailability_rules: When a domain is governed as NOT_READY_FOR_PRODUCTION or NOT_AVAILABLE, probability is null and operational decision is null. Platform must never interpret missing probability as low or zero risk.

input_contracts.architecture: Platform provides project/month context -> ML inference layer -> feature builder -> model -> platform-safe response. Platform does not calculate internal model features.
input_contracts.feature_engineering_boundary: Feature engineering (computing ratios, deltas, lags, stagnation flags, and missingness indicators) is an internal ML pipeline responsibility. Platform consumers provide source context and receive platform-safe prediction responses.

unified_profile.aggregation_prohibition_rule: STRICT PROHIBITION: Never construct a single mathematically combined overall risk probability (e.g. weighted sum, arithmetic/geometric mean, or max) across disparate risk domains. Each domain risk must be reported separately.
